title: My experience building an Arma/Wargame hybrid using Claude
author: pornhonked
selftext:
I note the rules on self-promotion, and I'm positing this purely to give information to others who might be building or trying to build a wargame or military simulation game using AI. My first commit was 40 days ago. There are 3,272 commits. I've used almost Opus 5.5 exclusively, with Fable 5.2 in the last couple of days, primarily for performance optimization. I develop on three PCs (one Claude instance per PC) plus a dedicated testing PC. I used ChatGPT Plus to refine the architecture ahead of any work in the code; ChatGPT developed the prompts for Claude. I am on a Claude Ultra plan and I've only run over my weekly allowance once.

The game is built in Three.js with custom code for most things. I tried to find existing libraries but in most cases I just paid Opus to do the work from scratch. The results are, I think, good.

Here's a video of me presenting the demo: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f9VGVStDojs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f9VGVStDojs)

The demo itself can be accessed directly at this link: [https://demo.woopi.workers.dev/](https://demo.woopi.workers.dev/)

Most of the first two weeks were spent building out little components to see what the AI could do. I was incredible impressed - within days I had world terrain data (DEM, OSM etc) being served from a web server into the app, and I was adding features on an hourly basis. The ability of the AI to build regression tests is incredible, but its not perfect (bugs still slip through the cracks). You need to be very disciplined and not rush - if you rush, the AI rushes, and this can lead to bugs.

My application now has over 500k lines of code and 4,200 tests. It does far more than the demo shows, and that's because it's the "polish" where the human comes in. I tweaked every button, and almost every tooltip. I only had time so far to polish what you see in the demo - the end to end workflow for scenario development, terrain development etc etc just isn't ready for prime time yet.

Tools: 99% of 3D models were procedurally generated by Claude. I used Meshy for the Osprey and F-35 you see in the demo (100k triangles each). Character models were bought through various web stores and converted by Claude. The animations were purchased and adapted to our animation system by Claude. I build many labs (animation lab, sound lab etc) to get things looking right before getting them into the game. I bought sounds as well - this was actually the most expensive, paying a dude on Fivver to make sound effects.

My background: programmer for a decade from 2004 to 2014, then "product management". I am very worried for all the talented young people who earn a living from programming, web development etc etc, there is no doubt in my mind that these people will be in trouble. I am genuinely concerned about the number of people who will lose their jobs in the coming months to years. I literally worked for a game development company with 450 people - I was the Chief Product Officer - I am terrified for most of these people, because the technology that took us years (and incredible talent) can be built by AI in days. I have concerns.

Anyway, ask questions if you like, and no I am not going to post the repos.
